pr_title: Implements indexer in DataDictionary derived classes
pr_body:
#### Description
Explicitly implements the indexer `this[string]` to all classed that inherit from `DataDictionary` since pythonnet was not able to access the indexer from the parent class.

- Changes DividentAlgorithm.py to test the fix.

#### Related Issue
Closes #2806

#### Motivation and Context
Lean API should be the same for C# and Python algorithm.

#### Requires Documentation Change
No.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
Regression tests.

issue_context.title: Accessing indexer in DataDictionary throws "unindexable object" error in python algorithms
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Python algorithm can access `DataDictionary` values through its indexer:

#### Actual Behavior
Accessing indexer in objects that inherits from `DataDictionary`, e.g. `Splits`,  throws `unindexable object` error in python algorithms

#### Potential Solution
Implements the indexer explicitly in classes that inherit from `DataDictionary`.

#### Reproducing the Problem
```spy_split = slice.Splits['SPY']```
#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue

review_comments: Maybe a note `<remarks></remarks>` in these added `this[string ticker]` implementations of why its required would be good for future us
